note: Trust matrix: 31 action categories x 5 trust levels. Decisions: auto, ask, blocked.
visual_capture_note: visual_capture (Session 11) asks at levels 1 AND 2, where read_files
auto-approves from level 2. A named file can be classified before it is
opened; a screen cannot — the frame may hold a bank portal, a password
manager or a password field with nothing in the caller's request to say
so. The step up to 3 is where the user has accepted that ZUZZ looks at
browser_note: The three browse_internet / web_automation / download_files rows are Phase 3
Step 2, and they are deliberately not the browse row's numbers with new
labels on them.
browse_internet is the only one that asks all the way up and hands over at 5.
A page is unreviewed content arriving from someone else, and the trust levels
below 5 are precisely the ones where the user has not yet said they are
happy for ZUZZ to read the internet unprompted. Note it is *stricter* than
browse, which auto-approves from 4: browse was written when browsing meant
'open a browser window for the user to look at', and there is nothing in that
for ZUZZ to get wrong. Fetching and reading a page is a different act.
web_automation sits where mouse_keyboard sits, asking to 2 and auto from 3.
A click in a page is a click on the world — it can send a message, place an
order, delete a document on a site ZUZZ is only reading. It is trusted exactly
as much as the user's own click and not one bit more, which is the whole
reason it is a separate row: it would be easy, and wrong, to let clicking
inherit browse's permission because 'the user already allowed the browsing'.
download_files asks at EVERY level, 5 included, and there is no row above it
because there should not be one. Trust level 5 is autonomy over ZUZZ's own
routine work, not permission to put unreviewed binaries on the disk without
being asked. The cost of asking here is one click, and the cost of not asking
is the thing every other row in this file exists to prevent.
system_awareness_note: system_awareness (Phase 3 Step 3, the Parietal Lobe) is auto at EVERY level,
and it is the one documented departure from level 1's "ask permission for
everything". Read it before changing the row.
It is not borrowing read_files because a window title is not a file. Reading
notes.txt shows the user what ZUZZ read; reading a title bar shows whatever
the open document happens to be called, which for a lot of people is a
customer, a salary, or the first line of something they have not finished
typing. That is why it is its own row: it is its own disclosure.
It is auto because the exposure is bounded in a way a screenshot's is not.
A screenshot can hold a rendered bank portal; a title is a few dozen
characters. More importantly the inference stays on this machine —
detect_context reduces a title to one of six words and it is the word, not
the title, that ever reaches the model. Making the user approve "ZUZZ may
read a window title" before it can answer "what am I working on" would
train them to click the button without reading it, which is the real cost
What this row does NOT cover: the gates still run. Every parietal_* call is
proposed, scored, audited and kill-switched like every other action, and a
decision for one operation cannot be replayed on another.
memory_note: memory_access (Phase 6, the Hippocampus) is auto at EVERY level, the same
documented departure from level 1's "ask permission for everything" that
system_awareness already makes. Read this before changing the row.
It does not borrow read_files, because memory is not a file read. Reading a
file shows the user exactly what ZUZZ read and the read ends. A recall can
surface a preference stated three months ago and act on it, and that is a
disclosure with a lifetime rather than a single read.
It is auto because the exposure is bounded and local: nothing in the region
sends anything off the machine, and the alternative is a dialog every time
ZUZZ says "as you mentioned" — which trains people to click prompts through.
That is the failure mode that makes prompts worse than having none. The
permission this row withholds is available on demand instead: the Memory
page lists every stored memory, and each one can be read and erased by hand.
THE ROW DOES NOT COVER ERASING, and that is the real trade-off. forget_before
is the only irreversible operation in the region and it runs at every level.
The counter-argument is that a machine which cannot forget holds a wrong
statement about its user forever with no recourse, which is its own kind of
harm. The mitigation is structural rather than permission-based: an
unreadable date is a refusal, never a silent "forget everything", so the
destructive direction always needs a real date from the caller.
code_note: The five Phase 4 rows, for body/mouth/kilo/. Read this before changing any of
them: the coding agents can write to a user's disk and can install software,
which makes this the first family whose strongest capability is unattended at
trust level 4.
generate_code and modify_project borrow mouse_keyboard's shape - ask at 1 and 2,
auto from 3. Producing source text is a read of the user's problem statement and
an act on nothing else; writing it into a user-designated workspace is a saved
bundle of file writes, so from the level where the user trusts ZUZZ with the
machine they trust it with their project. Neither can touch ZUZZ itself: that is
a refusal in body/mouth/kilo/kilo_workspace.py, not a permission level, because a
row cannot express 'anywhere except here'.
execute_code mirrors run_python exactly (auto only at 5) and git_operations sits
on the same row. Both run the user's code or rewrite their history; a generated
test suite that deletes fixtures is not a gentler act than one typed by hand, and
git can make unrecoverable commits unreachable.
install_packages asks at EVERY level, 5 included, alongside install_software,
download_files and delete_files. This is immutable rule R7 - never install
software without user approval - and a wheel runs whatever build hooks its author
wrote. An agent loop that can hallucinate a package name is exactly the actor R7
was written about, so trust level 5 being 'autonomy over routine work' does not
extend to it. The cost is one click per install.
routine_note: routine_management (Phase 6, the Basal Ganglia) borrows mouse_keyboard's
shape — ask at 1 and 2, auto from 3 — and that is the right neighbour.
A routine is a stored bundle of desktop acts. The user approved those acts
once each, and without them being bundled, so from the level where they trust
ZUZZ with the desktop they trust it with a saved sequence of desktop acts.
It does not auto-approve at the low levels even though listing and reading a
routine is harmless, because the category also covers writing them and the
matrix has no per-operation axis: a row loose for reading has to be loose for
writing too. Rewriting a routine at level 2 would be the assistant
reorganising its own authority rather than the user's housekeeping.
A routine is NEVER run on the strength of the decision that created it.
Every step is re-checked against this matrix at the trust level in force when
the routine executes, so storing one stores no permission. A routine built
at level 5 and run at level 1 does only what level 1 allows.
personality_note: personality_access (Phase 6, the Cerebellum) is auto at EVERY level, and is the
narrowest of the three Phase 6 rows. It reaches no file, no window title and no
other machine: it reads the register, detects the tone of one message, and moves
one knob that changes how ZUZZ's own replies are worded.
It does not auto-approve by assuming the write half is harmless. It does not need
to: the writable set is fixed in config/personality.json as editable_keys, and the
owner's name is not one of them, so a model cannot rename its user by calling
personality_update_setting. The bound is structural rather than permission-based,
which is the only kind that survives the row being changed.
A prompt here would cost more than it buys. ZUZZ dropping the filler because the
user sounds frustrated is the feature; asking first puts a dialog in front of
someone at the exact moment they least want to read one, and the answer to a
'may I sound less cheerful?' prompt is not a considered one.
response_enhancement_note: response_enhancement (Phase 4.5, Jarvis-style response enhancement) is auto at
EVERY level. It controls how ZUZZ's own replies are enhanced and presented:
thinking visualization, confidence scoring, context continuation, proactive
suggestions, self-critique, and mood-adaptive tone. These are read-only
presentation controls — they change how ZUZZ speaks, not what it does.
It is auto because the exposure is zero: no file, no window, no network, no
model input is affected. The tools only toggle UI behaviours. A prompt here
would be a dialog asking 'may I show you my reasoning?' — the answer is
always yes, and the dialog would only annoy.

3.description: Auto-approve mouse, keyboard and safe commands
